# The commands

Every call that reads or changes a database is also a command: a name
and one JSON object, answered by one JSON object. A command is how a
caller that is not a Go program reaches a document. The list is written
from the engine's own table, so it has every command and no other.

Today a command is run by the Go call `Exec`. The server that takes the
same commands over the network is in progress (Phase 6) and is not
built: nothing listens yet.

## A command and its answer

Ann's agent approves an invoice. The command is `transition`, and its
object says which document, which transition and what to write with it:

```json
{"class": "Invoice", "id": "FV/2026/11/0042", "transition": "approve",
 "values": {"note": "matches order PO-118"},
 "key": "approve-FV/2026/11/0042"}
```

The answer holds the document after the command, under `document`:

```json
{"document": {"class": "Invoice", "id": "FV/2026/11/0042", "title": "FV/2026/11/0042",
              "state": "approved", "version": 2, "class_version": 1,
              "created_at": 1794562200, "updated_at": 1794562200, "state_entered_at": 1794562200,
              "created_by": "bob", "updated_by": "ap-agent",
              "state_entered_by": "ap-agent", "state_entered_from": "review",
              "values": {"customer": "Customer:42", "note": "matches order PO-118"}}}
```

When the engine does not carry the command out, the answer holds the
refusal under `error`, with its code, its message and, where there is
one, a hint and the place. Bob, who is not in finance, sends the same
command:

```json
{"error": {"code": "forbidden",
           "message": "bob may not take approve from review",
           "hint": "the rule of approve: INGROUP(\"finance\")",
           "path": "/access/transition/approve"}}
```

[The refusals](refusals.md) lists every code. A definition that is
refused answers `bad_definition`, with every finding beside the error
under `diagnostics`.

## What holds for every command

- **Who calls is never in the command.** The caller comes with the door
  the command is sent through: in a Go program, the principal given to
  `Exec`. The one thing a command says about its caller is `for`, whom
  the caller acts for, and the engine lets that through only while a
  substitution says so.
- **A member the command does not take is refused**, with `bad_json`
  and the place of the member. So is a member given twice, a member of
  the wrong JSON type, and a command that lacks a member it needs. A
  member given as `null` is read as left out.
- **An answer names what it holds**: a document under `document`, a
  list under its plural, a count under its name. A list that is empty is
  `[]`.
- **A definition is read back as it was given.** `get_class`,
  `get_schema`, `get_table` and `get_action` answer the JSON a designer
  wrote under `definition`, with its `name`, its `version` and who
  `defined` it beside it, so that the definition can be changed and sent
  again as it is.

## The members that mean the same everywhere

A command takes the ones its list below shows, and no other.

| Member | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `key` | text | the idempotency key: the same command sent again with the same key makes no second commit and is answered as the first was |
| `business_date` | text | the business day of the commit, as "2026-11-13"; the server's day when left out |
| `reason` | text | why a content administrator acts past a rule of the class; kept on the event |
| `for` | text | the id of whoever the caller acts for; let through only while a substitution says so |
| `at` | moment | the moment the command reads at: "2026-11-13", "2026-11-13 09:30:00" in UTC, or seconds since the epoch; now when left out |

## Documents

| Command | What it does | |
|---|---|---|
| [`create`](#create) | Makes a document. | writes |
| [`create_many`](#create_many) | Makes several documents of one class in one transaction, all or none. | writes |
| [`get`](#get) | Reads a document. | reads |
| [`set`](#set) | Assigns values to a document and recalculates what depends on them. | writes |
| [`reset`](#reset) | Puts input variables of a document back to their defaults. | writes |
| [`refresh`](#refresh) | Recomputes triggered variables of a document, and lets it move if a guard on time now holds. | writes |
| [`transition`](#transition) | Moves a document along a named transition of its class. | writes |
| [`transition_many`](#transition_many) | Moves several documents of one class along one transition; a document that cannot move is reported and the others move. | writes |
| [`delete`](#delete) | Removes a document; its history and its events stay. | destroys |
| [`transitions`](#transitions) | Lists the transitions leaving a document's state, each with whether the caller may take it now. | reads |
| [`due`](#due) | Lists the documents of a class that a commit would move now: a guard on time holds, or a timer has come. | reads |
| [`history`](#history) | Reads every committed version of a document, oldest first. | reads |
| [`version`](#version) | Reads one committed version of a document. | reads |
| [`events`](#events) | Reads the events that touched a document, oldest first. | reads |
| [`preview`](#preview) | Runs a create, a set or a transition without writing anything. | reads |
| [`preview_delete`](#preview_delete) | Answers what a delete of a document would do, without deleting it. | reads |
| [`preview_many`](#preview_many) | Runs the batch transition_many would run, without writing anything. | reads |
| [`query`](#query) | Reads the documents of a class that match a filter. | reads |
| [`count`](#count) | Counts the documents of a class that match a filter. | reads |
| [`sql`](#sql) | Runs one read-only SELECT over the views, for an analyst. | reads |

### create

Makes a document. It writes; in Go it is the call `Create`.

| Member | Type | | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `class` | text | needed | the name of the class |
| `values` | object |  | the values to assign, by variable |
| `id` | text |  | the id of the new document; generated when left out |

And, of the members that mean the same everywhere: `key`, `business_date`, `reason`, `for`.

It answers:

| Member | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `document` | the new document |

| `documents` | list of objects | needed | the documents, each {"values": {…}} |

|---|---|---|---|

## Definitions

| Command | What it does | |
|---|---|---|
| [`define_class`](#define_class) | Defines a class, or the next version of one. | writes |
| [`define_classes`](#define_classes) | Defines several classes in one call, all or none: how classes that name each other are defined. | writes |
| [`define_schema`](#define_schema) | Defines a named schema of an object. | writes |
| [`define_table`](#define_table) | Defines a table of reference data. | writes |
| [`define_action`](#define_action) | Defines an action a rule may name. | writes |
| [`validate_class`](#validate_class) | Reports what define_class would refuse, storing nothing. | reads |
| [`validate_classes`](#validate_classes) | Reports what define_classes would refuse, storing nothing. | reads |
| [`validate_action`](#validate_action) | Reports what define_action would refuse, storing nothing. | reads |
| [`get_class`](#get_class) | Reads a class back as it was defined. | reads |
| [`get_schema`](#get_schema) | Reads a schema back as it was defined. | reads |
| [`get_table`](#get_table) | Reads a table's definition back as it was defined. | reads |
| [`get_action`](#get_action) | Reads an action's definition back as it was defined. | reads |
| [`list_classes`](#list_classes) | Lists the classes. | reads |
| [`list_schemas`](#list_schemas) | Lists the schemas. | reads |
| [`list_tables`](#list_tables) | Lists the tables. | reads |
| [`list_actions`](#list_actions) | Lists every action a rule may name, the engine's own first. | reads |
| [`definitions`](#definitions) | Lists the versions of one class, schema, table or action, with who defined each and when. | reads |
| [`preview_draft`](#preview_draft) | Tries a class definition that is not stored on a create, or on a document of the stored class of the same name, writing nothing. | reads |
| [`migrate`](#migrate) | Brings every live document of a class that an earlier version computed to the current version. | writes |

| Member | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `class` | the definition as it was given, with its name, its version and who defined it, and the notes of the class |

## Tables, actions and the queue

| Command | What it does | |
|---|---|---|
| [`table_rows`](#table_rows) | Reads every row of a table, in the order of its key. | reads |
| [`import_rows`](#import_rows) | Writes rows into a table; a row whose key exists is replaced. | writes |
| [`preview_action`](#preview_action) | Answers what an action would be called with, or the request it would send, with every secret masked; nothing is called or sent. | reads |
| [`try_action`](#try_action) | Runs an action once, outside any document; a request is sent for real. | writes |
| [`outbox`](#outbox) | Lists the actions commits queued: what waits, what ran and what is dead. | reads |
| [`retry_action`](#retry_action) | Makes a dead action pending again. | writes |
| [`drain`](#drain) | Runs every queued action that is due, now. | writes |
| [`check_blobs`](#check_blobs) | Recomputes the hash of every file the database holds. | reads |

### table_rows

Reads every row of a table, in the order of its key. It reads; in Go it is the call `TableRows`.

| Member | Type | | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `table` | text | needed | the name of the table |

And, of the members that mean the same everywhere: `at`, `for`.

It answers:

| Member | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `rows` | the rows, each an object of values by column |

### import_rows

Writes rows into a table; a row whose key exists is replaced. It writes; in Go it is the call `ImportRows`.

| Member | Type | | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `table` | text | needed | the name of the table |
| `rows` | list of objects | needed | the rows, each an object of values by column |
| `replace` | true or false |  | true empties the table first, so that the rows given are all its rows |

And, of the members that mean the same everywhere: `for`.

It answers:

| Member | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `imported` | how many rows it wrote |

### preview_action

Answers what an action would be called with, or the request it would send, with every secret masked; nothing is called or sent. It reads; in Go it is the call `PreviewAction`.

| Member | Type | | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | text | needed | the name of the action |
| `args` | object |  | its arguments, by parameter |

And, of the members that mean the same everywhere: `for`.

It answers:

| Member | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `preview` | the call, or the request |

### try_action

Runs an action once, outside any document; a request is sent for real. It writes; in Go it is the call `TryAction`.

| Member | Type | | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | text | needed | the name of the action |
| `args` | object |  | its arguments, by parameter |

And, of the members that mean the same everywhere: `for`.

It answers:

| Member | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `outcome` | what the action returned, or how it failed |

### outbox

Lists the actions commits queued: what waits, what ran and what is dead. It reads; in Go it is the call `Outbox`.

| Member | Type | | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `status` | text |  | pending, done or dead; every status when left out |
| `class` | text |  | only the actions of documents of this class |
| `id` | text |  | only the actions of this document |
| `limit` | whole number |  | the most actions to answer |

And, of the members that mean the same everywhere: `for`.

It answers:

| Member | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `actions` | the actions, in the order they were queued |

### retry_action

Makes a dead action pending again. It writes; in Go it is the call `RetryAction`.

| Member | Type | | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action_key` | text | needed | the key of the queued action, as outbox lists it |

And, of the members that mean the same everywhere: `for`.

It answers `{}`.

### drain

Runs every queued action that is due, now. It writes; in Go it is the call `Drain`.

It takes nothing of its own; of the members that mean the same everywhere, `for`.

It answers:

| Member | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `attempted` | how many actions it attempted |

### check_blobs

Recomputes the hash of every file the database holds. It reads; in Go it is the call `CheckBlobs`.

It takes nothing of its own; of the members that mean the same everywhere, `for`.

It answers:

| Member | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `checked` | how many files it checked |
| `mismatched` | the hashes of the files whose bytes do not match |

## What is not a command

A few calls of the Go package have no command.

| Call | Why |
|---|---|
| `Action` | it answers one entry of the catalogue that list_actions answers whole |
| `Class` | it answers the engine's compiled form to a Go program; get_class answers the definition |
| `Close` | closing a database is for the program that opened it |
| `Exec` | it is the door the commands come through |
| `OpenBlob` | the bytes of a file are not JSON: they travel beside the commands, with the server |
| `OpenFile` | the bytes of a file are not JSON: they travel beside the commands, with the server |
| `PutBlob` | the bytes of a file are not JSON: they travel beside the commands, with the server |
| `Schema` | it answers the engine's compiled form to a Go program; get_schema answers the definition |
| `Table` | it answers the engine's compiled form to a Go program; get_table answers the definition |
